newsitem.title: LEBANON: Rostropovich concert symbolises Lebanon recovery.
newsitem.headline: Rostropovich concert symbolises Lebanon recovery.

text.p: Russian cellist Mstislav Rostropovich marked the return of peace to Lebanon by performing amid the towering Roman columns of Baalbek, near the cells where Western hostages were imprisoned a decade ago.
The concert, on Wednesday night before 2,500 spectators, came hours after the United States announced it was ending a 10-year-old ban on its own citizens visiting Lebanon.

The performance was the highlight of the first Baalbek Festival since 1974. The festival, held in the spectacular Roman ruins of Baalbek, was an annual event until the 15-year Lebanese civil war began in 1975.

"I am very excited because for me it is a very important day as peace comes for my beloved country and beloved friends," Rostropovich, 70, said before the concert in front of the temple of Jupiter in Lebanon's eastern Bekaa valley.
"I am honoured to play at this fanastic day and such a fantastic place," he said before performing the Dvorak cello concerto with the orchestra of Radio France.

Baalbek had become a no-go area for Westerners during the 1980s when it was a stronghold of the militant Islamic movement Hizbollah, blamed by the United States for kidnappings in which Western hostages were held for years.
Terry Anderson, the last American to be freed, was held in Baalbek for a large part of the 2,545 days he was a hostage before his release in December 1991.
"This event in particular has a meaning because Rostropovich performed here nearly 25 years ago and now he is playing in the same place," said spectator Abedo Basha.
